question.problem:
The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{2{x}^{3}-1}{{x}^{5}-2x}$ is

$y=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2{x}^{3}-1}{{x}^{5}-2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})}{(1-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{0-0}{1-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$
